story: A giant being was said to be the creation figure, sleeping within an egg of chaos. As he awoke, he stood up and divided the sky from the earth. He then died after standing up, and his body turned into rivers, mountains, plants, animals, and everything else in the world, among which was a powerful being. This powerful being gave birth to a twin brother and sister, who had human faces and the bodies of snakes. The two lived together on a mythical mountain. One day they set up two separate piles of fire, and the flames eventually became one; taking this as a sign, they decided to become husband and wife. They used clay to create offspring, and with divine power they made the clay figures come alive, and these became the earliest human beings. The brother looked upward and studied the images in the heavens, and looked downward and studied the occurrences on earth. He united husband and wife and laid down the laws of humanity, devising eight symbolic figures made of two fundamental forces in order to gain mastery over the world, representing heaven, earth, water, fire, thunder, wind, mountain, and lake. He taught people to cook food and to hunt and fish, including fishing with nets and hunting with weapons of bone, wood, and bamboo. He instituted marriage and the family structure and offered the first sacrifices to the sky. He is said to have received the pattern for his symbols from markings on the back of a dragon-horse (or tortoise) that emerged from a river, an event said to be the origin of writing. He is also credited with inventing a stringed musical instrument. His daughter, also said to be his consort, drowned while crossing a river and became its spirit. He is said to have lived 197 years and to have died in a place where a monument to him still stands.
